## What happened

During validation before selecting `V1-SM05`, the Judge found unresolved project setup gaps and
confirmed that the project remains in `SETUP-SPIKE-000`. Closing the S2–S4 scorecards did not end the
setup container for this purpose. The Judge directed Lane A to:

1. record exactly which `D-257` and `D-258` clauses change;
2. identify every blocker, owner, acceptance proof and return condition; and
3. raise the `V1-SM05` packet status to **`BLOCKED`** in Phase 1;
4. preserve the completed pre-selection Lane A handoff-validation checklist as historical attempt
   `SV-001`, without calling it a `V1-SM05` feature DoR/DoD run;
5. create setup-validation attempt `SV-002` for the new findings and record its drift from `SV-001`;
   and
6. reserve the first `V1-SM05` feature DoR/DoD run for after selection, when Lane B creates the first
   behavioral test code; and
7. separate the reusable, versioned DoR/DoD template from each immutable attempt run, with the
   template covering Project, Product, execution scope, backlog refinement and relevant historical
   dialogue/tooling before an attempt can close.

This is authorization to prepare and apply the bounded governance package. It is not authorization to
construct SM05, install an unreviewed tool or treat Lane C's suggested remedies as already proven.

### Tracking chain carried by the template — existing authorities preserved

Judge clarification 5 requires every validation template to trace from global tracking through the
bounded attempt. This is a **coverage chain**, not a replacement authority hierarchy. Each section
reads its existing canonical owner and the Register still arbitrates conflicts:

| Required template scope | Canonical sources | What every attempt records |
|---|---|---|
| **Project** | Frozen Project PRD and Charter; Register, Build Spec and Inventory under `D-54`/`D-58` | Project constraint IDs, applicability, current decision, evidence and unresolved transfers |
| **Product** | `Modular_PRD`, relevant Fn_Specs and SPECS under `D-29` | Product/module/version requirement IDs, behavior affected, scope exclusions, and every MMF in the gate's declared scope with selection status and dependency disposition |
| **Execution scope** | The setup packet or selected MMF packet and bounded work order | Exact target scope ID, gate, packet, child unit, acceptance behavior and authorization state |
| **Backlog refinement** | `docs/handoff/` under `D-90` and each entry's weakest-child state | Every relevant Open, Deferred or returned item, its relevance decision, owner, proof and return condition |
| **Historical dialogue and tooling** | Decisions, prior attempts, receipts and relevant agent/tool findings | Source reference, what was asserted, what was proven, what changed and the current disposition |
| **Attempt lineage** | Immutable attempt records and their drift ledgers | Template version, prior attempt, result, evidence index and destination receipts |

“All historical dialogue” means every record selected by an explicit inclusion rule: include any
decision, handoff child, receipt or tooling finding whose `Blocks`, `Follow-up-Tier`, return trigger,
affected artifact or acceptance behavior intersects the gate being run. The attempt lists included
items and excluded candidates with a reason. It does not copy conversation prose or turn a current
handoff tally into governed truth.

The chain therefore improves completeness while preserving these boundaries: handoffs remain lateral;
dialogue remains provenance; Graphify and the Encyclopedia remain searchable projections; and tools or
models gain no authority from appearing in the historical section.

The closure correction is one narrow invariant:

> A setup attempt may close only when its bounded children have terminal dispositions **and** every
> unresolved item has an accepted disposition or a named destination, owner, acceptance proof and
> return condition. The destination must record receipt before the source attempt claims transfer.

This invariant repairs the `D-258` failure without creating a duplicate master ledger.

## Versioned template and immutable attempt model

### Reusable template — specification, not a run

Lane A creates and inventories this reusable template:

> `docs/v1/work-packets/templates/DOR-DOD-VALIDATION-v1.md`

Its identity is `dor-dod-validation/v1`. It contains the required Project, Product, execution-scope,
backlog-refinement, historical-dialogue/tooling and attempt-lineage sections above; the closure
transfer invariant; the standard DoR and DoD evidence fields; and a DoR→DoD mapping table. It contains
no attempt result, checked gate, packet status or evidence claim.

Every attempt pins `Template-ID`, `Template-Version` and the template file's SHA-256 digest. A digest
is used instead of the containing commit because a new template and its first attempt may land in the
same governed pass; making that attempt cite the commit being created would be a self-reference. Once
an attempt uses version 1, Lane A does not edit that template version; a material template change
creates version 2. New template versions do not rewrite prior attempt results.

### Attempt lineage — discrete runs of a pinned template

`DOR-R1`–`DOR-R7` remain checked and keep their evidence, but their correct meaning is **completed
pre-selection Lane A handoff validation**. They tested the alignment of governed requirements,
behavioral scenarios and the Jev readiness script before selection. They did not run feature behavior
against application code and were not acceptance tests.

Lane A records this attempt lineage without clearing, copying or re-running the historical rows:

| Attempt | Template | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SV-001` | `legacy/embedded` — no retroactive v1 claim | Complete, historical | Retrospective wrapper for the completed `DOR-R1`–`DOR-R7` pre-selection handoff-validation record and its Jev readiness evidence; references the original rows without duplicating them |
| `SV-002` | `dor-dod-validation/v1`, pinned at creation | DoR open | First run of the new reusable template; created because the selection gate exposed untransferred setup gaps |
| `V1-SM05-FV-001` | Current accepted `dor-dod-validation/*`, pinned at creation | Not created | Unrun shell created by Lane A after selection/work-order authorization and before lane transfer; first run starts after active Lane B creates behavioral test code |

Lane A creates two attempt artifacts:

>

### Required success-drift comparison

The historical tag does not convert `SV-001` from Complete to Failed. It records two truths together:
the attempt completed the checklist and evidence expected at that time, and later validation exposed a
coverage/transfer defect in that checklist. `SV-002` measures whether the new template and transfer
rule correct that defect.

`SV-001.md` records `Outcome-At-Time: Complete`, its exact gate claim, the evidence that supported it,
and `Later-Observed-Limitations`. `SV-002.md` then compares these dimensions:

| Success-drift dimension | `SV-001` baseline | `SV-002` success criterion | Required classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope coverage | Existing `DOR-R1`–`DOR-R7` and Jev readiness sources | Project, Product/MMF, execution, backlog and relevant historical-dialogue indexes are complete, with explicit exclusions | `Improved`, `Unchanged`, `Regressed`, `Newly visible` or `Not comparable` |
| Transfer completeness | Terminal setup children without an item-level destination receipt | Every unresolved relevant item has disposition or destination, owner, proof, return condition and receipt | Same classification plus evidence link |
| Evidence strength | Evidence accepted for the earlier gate | Each `SV2-U*` result is reproducible, independently reviewed where required and pinned to a revision | Same classification plus evidence link |
| Blocker disposition | Later setup blockers were not all visible in the attempt | `SV2-U01`–`SV2-U04` each meets its return condition or retains an explicit blocking state | Same classification plus evidence link |
| Gate result | Pre-selection validation appeared complete and State-1 objects were created | The attempt refuses setup closure and SM05 selection while any required scope or transfer remains unresolved | Same classification plus observed gate result |
| Discovery timing | Missing items surfaced at the SM05 selection check | Equivalent gaps are surfaced inside `SV-002` before any lift/select act | Same classification plus discovery point |

The comparison has no averaged score: one unresolved required dimension keeps the attempt open under
the weakest-child and closure-transfer rules. Future attempts compare with their immediate predecessor
and retain `SV-001` as the historical baseline for long-range drift.

### Separate post-selection `V1-SM05` feature run

After selection and before transferring the commit lock, Lane A creates an **unrun shell** for
`V1-SM05-FV-001` from the current accepted `dor-dod-validation/*` template and pins its version and
SHA-256 digest. Its status is `Awaiting behavioral-test evidence`; no DoR or DoD result is recorded.
Lane B then becomes `Active` and creates the first behavioral test code under the bounded work order.
That code and Lane B's handoff start the first actual feature DoR/DoD run:

1. **Feature DoR passes** when the behavioral test code exists and its identifiers, inputs, expected
   outputs and exclusions align with the selected contract.
2. **Feature DoD fails on the first run** because those behavioral tests must be Red before the
   application behavior is constructed. That expected failure is recorded as test-first evidence,
   not as setup drift.
3. Lane B records the test identifiers, command and Red evidence in its owned code/test surface and
   handoff; it does not edit Lane A's attempt file. Lane B constructs the authorized behavior and
   records later Green evidence against the same attempt identity. When the lock returns, Lane A
   updates the attempt record from that handoff and performs its independent verification.

The Jev handoff-alignment script, the feature behavioral tests and the later customer acceptance run
may share canonical behavior IDs, but they are separate evidence classes. Alignment of documents and
test definitions cannot substitute for executing acceptance behavior against built code.

**The semantic expected set, kept separate from the three audit text matches:**

- **Criterion (1).** The candidate passes if the files and call sites it reports equal these sets, with no extra
  file or call site.
- **Path comparison.** Repo-relative paths, `\` normalized to `/`. A line number is compared only for call sites.
- **An import is not a caller.** Reporting the import as a caller is a false result.

**Measurement.**
- **What is measured:** the complete consumer-visible result of **one** invocation.
  - CLI: the raw stdout bytes.
  - MCP: the concatenated `text` items of the tool result, encoded as UTF-8.
- **Bytes:** byte length. **Characters:** Unicode code points of the UTF-8 decode.
- **Both limits apply:** bytes ≤ **221** (the raw baseline) **and** characters ≤ 12,000.
- **Empty versus error:** exit 0 or 1 with empty stdout and empty stderr is an empty result. Any other exit, or any
  stderr, is an error result. An error is recorded as an error and never counted as empty.
- **No post-filtering.** Arguments are chosen from discovery (R4) before any task output is seen. Raw output is
  kept as returned; nothing is trimmed after an over-budget result.

**Byte risk, not a result.** 221 bytes is a tight limit. The trial has not run, so no failure is established. Only a
Judge act may change the criterion, and that act must show the raw result and the effect of the change.

### P1 — Result classification (replaces the "Empty versus error" rule in R3)

Ripgrep's exit codes classify **the baseline only**. They do not carry over to the candidate.

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1. Freeze the rules at discovery | Before the task runs, record each interface's success, no-match and error rules from its `--help`, its MCP `tools/list` and the tool's input/output schema. Record the source of each rule. A rule with no source is **unknown** |
| 2. CLI | **Success:** the exit status that discovery documents as success, with stderr recorded. **No-match:** only the status or output that discovery documents as no-match. **Error:** any other status; a crash; a timeout (60 s per call); stderr that discovery documents as an error. If the rules are unknown, a non-zero status is an error, and an empty output with an unknown status is **inconclusive** |
| 3. MCP | Retain the **complete** JSON-RPC response (request, response, `isError`, every content item of every type). **Error:** a transport or protocol failure, a JSON-RPC `error`, `isError: true`, or a timeout. **Unsupported / inconclusive:** a content item that is not `text`, or that discovery does not explain. **Measured content:** the `text` items in order, UTF-8, frozen at discovery before the task |
| 4. Negative control | Empty passes **only** when the request is classified **success** or **no-match** under step 1. An error, an inconclusive result or an unknown status never passes |
| 5. Record | Each call records its classification, the rule applied and that rule's source |

### P2 — Cleanup proof (replaces "Disposable" and the removal proof in R4)

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1. Locate storage | During discovery, read `--help` and the documentation for cache, configuration or data locations and for options that redirect them. Where an option exists, point it at the scratch folder |
| 2. Record before | Before the first run, list and hash each **trial-owned location**: the extraction folder, the scratch cache, any documented default location, the repository (`git status --porcelain --ignored`), Lane B's MCP configuration and Lane C's skill folder |
| 3. Record after | After cleanup, record the same list and hashes. Each location must equal its before state, or hold only retained evidence |
| 4. Limit | An undocumented location that the checks cannot see is not proven clean. Report it as **cleanup incomplete: location not accounted for**. Do not claim a guarantee beyond the locations checked |
| 5. Do not touch | Pre-existing or unrelated files are never deleted. Retained evidence is copied out before cleanup and must survive it |

### Layer 2 — Sentinel design: what is supported and what must change

**Accept the method as a design candidate.** Known-present files removed during a controlled startup are stronger
evidence than files absent throughout. The pinned source supports the intended effect: `ponytail-activate.js`
L31–35 calls `clearMode()` for `off`, and `ponytail-runtime.js` L68–71 attempts to unlink its two resolved state files.
Neither this source reading nor r3's publication means the method has run or passed.

The current oracle is incomplete. r3 records intended sentinel content/hashes but does not explicitly require read-back
proof that both files exist just before launch, bound observations before any prompt/later hook, or refusal on an
unexplained intervening deletion. It admits another deleter can cause a false pass. Keep that attribution limit; do not
turn the phrase "both gone" alone into proof that SessionStart ran.

**Draft replacement for r11 §3 / §5 (design only):**

1. After G2 exits, O records the quiet-host condition and verifies the exact plain `D_C` paths and parent directories.
   Refuse a pre-existing flag, link/junction, wrong project-key path or a target outside `D_C`; never overwrite a file.
2. O creates the two explicitly allocated sentinels and reads back their exact content/hash and presence. Bind the
   attempt, expected project key, source/component identities and pre-launch time. A missing pre-launch proof refuses.
3. Start one fresh S-T session. O observes startup completion from plain PowerShell **before the first user prompt or
   any later hook/cleanup operation**. Bind this observation to that session and a defined startup deadline. Until this
   observation is complete, O makes no other write and no trial starts. Timeout/read error/ambiguous interval stops.
4. Both known-present sentinels absent, default-root protected projection unchanged, and the controlled interval
   accounted for are the proposed positive routing result, within the stated attribution limit. Either remains, only
   one disappears, or an unexplained deletion occurs: routing is unknown/failed and the unit stops. Do not delete a
   remaining sentinel and retry as if it had passed; preserve the failure for the authorized close ledger.
5. T-P0 remains the first S-T tool action after O's external startup observation. Replace §5's unqualified "sentinel
   test, then T-P0" with this actor/order distinction. Allocate the two sentinel additions/deletions explicitly in the
   phase map and capture/comparator contract; they grant no exception for other `D_C` or default-root changes.

The source table must also reflect `ponytail-runtime.js` L35–55: runtime host markers can override `getClaudeDir()`,
and the project key hashes normalized `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. Bind the expected resolved targets; do not describe the
single fallback line as the whole runtime. A remaining sentinel establishes failure to prove the required effect,
not a unique diagnosis of its cause. Routing evidence is specific to this startup; it is not every hook's environment
or loaded-component completeness.

**Planned controls, not run here:** correct startup deletion; both already absent/missing pre-proof; wrong root or hook
not run; one file remains; wrong project key; pre-existing/link/outside target; unaccounted later deletion or observation
after a prompt; lookup error. Only the first valid controlled case may pass. r3 §8 currently lists only removal/remains/
outside-target cases. Complete the refusal contract before candidate implementation.

### Layer 2 — Remaining gaps and concrete fixes

**BCP2-R1 — a filtered object ID is not a raw-byte oracle.** Map r2 §C says `git hash-object <file>` equals the pinned
blob proves byte equality. `.gitattributes` declares Markdown `text eol=lf`. Git's default file hashing can apply
those filters. A read-only control with synthetic LF and CRLF stdin buffers, using `--path=docs/PRD.md`, produced the
same filtered object ID `bc8bc4ec53e20f9cab6c7fff61afdc2d6ed59563`. With `--no-filters`, the CRLF input instead produced
`2dcb9e2ad4180418c51d2fb43c4953e66056a306`. The raw SHA-256 values also differed. No frozen file or Git object was written.
The [Git manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-hash-object) confirms that `--no-filters` disables attribute and line-ending
conversion. Thus the stated oracle would miss a byte change consisting only of these line endings.

**Draft replacement for the map's frozen-proof cell:**

> Compare `git hash-object --no-filters -- <file>` with `git rev-parse <pinned-commit>:<repo-relative-path>`, requiring
> both commands to succeed; or compare the working bytes directly with the bytes from `git cat-file blob` for that
> pinned object. Record the pin, result and observer. An error or mismatch refuses. No `-w` option. Source-sweep
> separately checks existence and last-touch history; it is not this byte check.

Lane B repeated both the unfiltered-object and direct-buffer comparisons for PRD (`53ace36`), Charter (`00d21cd`)
and `0001` (`53ace36`): **all three match**. This finding corrects the general proof contract, not current file damage.
Keep Lane A's prior observation as attributed history; do not relabel a filtered check as one it did not run.

**BCP2-R2 — external custody still uses an unnamed owner.** Map r2 §C combines T2–T5 under “owning lane” for writer
and recovery. That leaves no named custodian and mixes immutable evidence, versioned proposals and live trial copies.
Use these scoped rows in the same map; this is the remaining part of the existing per-output preservation request:

### Layer 2 — Ripwire: app-source scope is not host isolation

**Current authority:** Register D-433 §5.14e258 item 1 (L28045 onward) and FN §4.4 select the existing route. The
retained U03 result is not a generic prohibition on all future evaluation. A new scoped trial still needs its own
selection and must address the earlier failed criteria; merely moving docs does not satisfy those criteria.

`my-editorial-app` implementation corpus. It is not the parent directory containing both repositories. The source
boundary excludes the canonical docs repository, credentials and unrelated host state. Its task manifest names
required code, SQL, test and build/workflow-dependency roots. Ownership is not a read restriction: Lane C must still
trace a workflow into Lane A scripts/config and Lane B tests. A required empty/missing root is incomplete scope,
never no-match; an optional exclusion needs a reason before the search (AIG-04.R4).

|---|---|

| Measurement | One named consumer task, baseline, negative control, SQL fallback and host-specific result. A later authorized boundary control must demonstrate exclusion of the docs tree and detect an unexpected write; code discovery is not behavior proof |

0.6.3 result and current upstream documentation are different evidence; do not combine them into one passed trial.

### Layer 3 — Proposed two-repository file contract

**Recommendation for design review:** keep one project authority chain and separate storage by purpose. Lane A
still owns rules, scripts and build configuration that must execute in the app repository. Lane B owns application
code; Lane C owns app workflows. All three need the approved reading routes. Separate repositories do not by
themselves provide a filesystem sandbox, prevent host-profile changes or authorize simultaneous Active lanes.

`<DOCS>` means the proposed docs repository; `<APP>` means the existing app repository. Every path in this table is
a design target, not a move instruction. Lane A must reconcile each existing F/P/T row to one canonical owner.

| Artifact / proposed destination | Producer, consumer and rule | Acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `<DOCS>/docs/PRD.md`, `docs/source/project-charter-v1.md`, `docs/Modular_PRD.md`, `docs/fn-specs/`, `docs/specs/`, `docs/v1/`, handoffs and templates | Candidate canonical intent/tracking home. Lane A records governed changes; Lane B/C retain their handoff/review roles. Frozen inputs keep exact bytes. Existing app sources remain authoritative until a recorded cutover | Old-path -> new-path map, original repository/commit/blob provenance, all references and history-dependent checks accounted for; no competing editable Register |
| `<APP>/app/`, `lib/`, `components/`, `supabase/`, `__tests__/` | Lane B, under work order. Frozen `0001_init.sql` remains here unchanged; code and schema are not moved into the docs repo | App commit, tests and requirement/AC references tied to the consumed intent revision |
| `<APP>/scripts/`, build config, `.githooks/`, agent rule/load files and local operational control docs | Lane A. Files required to run app checks stay executable from the app checkout. For example `.github/WORKFLOWS-SPEC.md` needs an explicit retain/move disposition, not automatic movement because it is Markdown | Per-file owner and location; tested loader/check route; generated rule copies, if chosen, are bound projections, not independently edited policy |
| `<APP>/.github/workflows/` | Lane C; Lane A supplies referenced scripts/config; Lane B supplies tests | Workflow input/source revision, entry-point and later runtime evidence under the existing phase allocation |
| `<DOCS>/.specify/` and `<DOCS>/specs/<feature-id>/` | **Spec Kit candidate workspace only.** Lane A proposes exact integration/version and managed paths. Outputs are drafts until mapped and accepted into the existing hierarchy | Pinned source/templates, command-by-command reads/writes, conflict/upgrade/restore map. `specs/` and canonical `docs/specs/` must never be conflated |
| `<APP>/docs/intent-lock.json` plus `<APP>/.governance/intent/<docs-commit>/` | Proposed lock and immutable consumer projection. Lane A defines the format; Lane B consumes. Use a reviewed export of necessary intent, no moving branch lookup and no second editable authority | Docs repo identity/full commit; each artifact ID/path/anchor/raw hash; decision/work-order/receipt IDs; allowed projection paths; refuse missing input or mismatch |
| `<DOCS>/docs/verification/<unit>/<run>.json` | Proposed return receipt. Executing lane supplies the app result; Lane A records governed conclusions and handoff lifecycle rules remain | App repo/full commit; consumed docs commit; test/control IDs; result/log hashes, limits and independent review. A receipt never rewrites the original result |
| `<DOCS>/docs/graph-fragments/` and local `<DOCS>/.graphify/` | Proposed intent graph home, only after its own migration design. Existing graph remains in place now; code navigation is separate | Guard identity, history, source paths, receipt route and coverage/drift checks adapted and reviewed before use; no old `.graphify/` state copied as proof of freshness |

The lock/export route is a proposed explicit adapter. It is not a claim that unmodified Spec Kit supports this
two-repository workflow. Upstream's [existing-project guide](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/existing-projects.html)
describes initialization in one project root and warns of managed-path replacement. Its
[PowerShell resolver](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/scripts/powershell/common.ps1) uses `.specify/`
and can accept `SPECIFY_INIT_DIR`; selecting that root proves neither the agent's implementation destination nor
write isolation. Pin and inspect the actual selected integration before relying on either behavior.

**Spec Kit adapter map:** constitution -> a derived view of the frozen hierarchy, Register and shared rules;
feature spec -> FN requirements/ACs; technical plan/data/contracts -> necessary SPECS and proposed app interfaces;
tasks -> a proposed work-order breakdown; implementation/tests -> app files under the issued work order; findings
and results -> the return receipt and B-series parent. None overrides D-29/D-58, turns a generated tasks file into
execution authority, or supplies missing acceptance evidence. Keep history according to the project's existing
D-36 distinction between version tracking and living specs, rather than importing an upstream persistence model
unchanged. Upstream also separates tool refresh from feature-spec evolution:
[artifact evolution guide](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/evolving-specs.html).

### Layer 4 — Chain, failure cases and the Chief Editor's decisions

**Forward:** approved intent at docs commit D -> app lock consumes D -> issued work order -> app commit A and tests.
**Backward:** app evidence at A identifies D and the affected requirement -> a finding/receipt in a later docs commit
E -> Lane A classifies the finding and records any authorized intent change -> a later app unit explicitly consumes
the new intent. E may cite A without changing D. Do not demand that D and A contain each other's final commit IDs;
that would create a circular hash dependency. A receipt-only docs commit is not an automatic change to the accepted
intent baseline. Branch names or an unversioned sibling-folder path are not this link.

| Gap / failure condition | Draft fix and success criterion |
|---|---|
| Docs are moved while controls still read old paths/history | Inventory the rule imports, `docs-drift`, coverage, source-sweep, terminal-return and guarded receipt lookup. `guarded-rebuild.mjs:2182` currently searches B-050 in the same Git repository. Preserve required original objects or define a reviewed cross-repository history/receipt route. Migration passes only when both consumers resolve exact sources and required checks do not silently SKIP |
| Two editable constitutions/Registers disagree | One canonical precedence and lane-state source. Local agent views are generated/pinned; any contradiction refuses the unit. A repository split changes storage, not the existing one-Active-lane rule |
| Spec Kit commands run in the docs repo but implementation is expected in the app repo | Specify the working directory, integration, input projection and permitted write roots for every command. Demonstrate the adapter later; do not infer it from the presence of `.specify/` |
| An app-only search is treated as a full project review | Name source scope and excluded corpus in every result. Review intent through the pinned docs inputs; preserve SQL and workflow dependency checks in app navigation |
| Installation isolation is inferred from repository separation | Bind profile/config/cache effects independently. A later isolation test must observe the declared boundary; naming two repositories is not proof |
| The two repositories advance independently without a receipt | Pin the pair D/A and retain both histories/results. Change the consumed baseline only through an explicit reviewed unit; preserve the last accepted pair for recovery |

| Decision, parent first | Accept for the next phase when | Reject / defer when |
|---|---|---|
| BCP-ISO design | Lane A supplies the per-file allocation and the complete D -> A -> E chain | The answer only repeats tool adoption labels or assigns whole repos by lane |
| Repo topology (Judge, later) | Reviewed two-repo migration, control/history plan, affected tiers and recovery are concrete | No source pin, duplicate authority, unresolved consumer path or changed phase/lane rule hidden in a file move |
| Spec Kit adoption (Judge, separate) | A pinned adapter and all managed outputs map to the hierarchy without loss or extra authority | Default folders or tool convergence are treated as approved destinations or Gate 2 proof |
| Ripwire reconsideration (Judge, separate) | A named consumer need/return reason, pinned host route and bounded trial criteria address D-433 | Corpus separation alone is presented as proof that the earlier failed criteria now pass |
| SM05 entry | Its existing setup, selection, work-order and gate conditions are met | New tool/repository paperwork is substituted for those conditions |

**Lane evidence limits:** Lane A must answer with paths and production methods, not just names. Lane B must propose
the app input/output contract and review the design; it cannot claim runtime isolation now. Lane C must review any
changed workflow checkout/path contract and later measure its affected host. The old C-a result remains bounded
historical evidence; this proposal contains no new Lane C approval. The Chief Editor decides topology and adoption
separately after the packet is concrete. No decision request is needed to finish the present drafting.

### Layer 5 — One Lane A follow-up and stop point

1. Receive `340f70d` and this BCP-ISO extension together. Preserve accepted r6 facts; answer the existing R1/R2/pointer
   return once, with T2/T5 expanded by the boundaries above.
2. Draft one repository allocation/adapter section in the existing BCP-1 packet. Join its rows to the F/P/T IDs.
   Bind exact repository identities, tool pins and every proposed file; mark unbound values as open.
3. Add the D -> A -> E specimen, per-command effects, migration/history/graph impacts and recovery to that same
   packet. Retain current canonical sources and all prior evidence. Draft only: no repo creation, moves, installs,
   settings changes, tool execution, generated control files, governed edits or graph rebuild.
4. Record one Lane A answer with the packet hash and delta. Lane B reviews the contract; seek Lane C evidence for
   changed workflow/host claims at the applicable review point. Then present the bounded topology/adoption choices
   to the Judge. Continue independent drafting; no extra acknowledgement cycle or duplicate handoff is required.

**Drift scope:** this is an appended handoff proposal. The governed graph remains analysed at `b308d1c`; no source
move or source edit has occurred. A later approved migration would affect governed sources and the graph/control
contract and needs its guarded route. It cannot reuse today's handoff-only drift conclusion. Checks and evidence
for this review are retained in `C:/CoWork/outputs/lane-b-bcp-isolation-2026-10-15/`.

| Verdict | Item | Condition / follow-up phase |
|---|---|---|
| **Approve** | The missing distinction between tool status, corpus scope, host effects and repository authority | Phase 1: clarify T2/T5 and keep prior evidence |
| **Approve-with-conditions** | App-source boundary and two-repository architecture as design candidates | Phase 1: complete the allocation, adapter, revision chain and migration proof plan; Lane B reviews |
| **Defer** | Topology cutover; Spec Kit adoption; Ripwire trial/provision; actual isolation and workflow evidence | Separate later bounded decisions and execution; no inferred SM05 gate |
| **Reject** | Repo-per-lane ownership by implication; two repos called a sandbox; duplicate live authority; automatic adoption or readiness from folder names | Phase 1: use the explicit contracts above |

| Executable behavior cases in B-owned __tests__/ and required test fixtures | Phase 2 starts after the authorized entry above; B selects the fitting xDD method under D-242 | Test IDs, exact source ACs, runner/environment and failing-first reason; an infrastructure failure does not prove missing behavior |
| specs/<feature-id>/spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md | Phase 2, after the bounded behavior-test baseline is recorded; precise lane allocation must exist before writing | B's implementation contract and work breakdown; reference the intent revision and test IDs/results, then guide the application changes |
| app/, lib/, components/ and authorized supabase/ changes | Phase 2, under that implementation contract and work order | Implemented behavior, passing child/regression/integration evidence and local database replay where required |
| Existing V1-SM05-FV-001 tracking/evidence destination | Create after selection; run only once behavioral test code exists, as the current SM05 packet states | Failing-first and later passing evidence toward feature DoD; exact path/custodian follows the existing packet, not a new duplicate ledger |
| .specify/ plus selected integration files | Shared support for the Phase 2 workflow; A provisions under a separate bounded tool/control act before B needs it | Tool/control availability and source-rule/provisioning trace, tracked separately from product-behavior completion proof |

Do not classify every file under docs/ as Phase 1 work: the existing work packet and feature-run records there
also track Phase 2 evidence. Keep their established destinations. Partition the tracking rows by their obligation,
phase, producer and evidence state; do not move them merely to make the folder names look consistent.

**The two parent relationships:** approved intent is the authority parent; executable behavior cases are the
verification reference; specs/ is the implementation parent for the application changes. A test observation
cannot amend intent. The trace is intent ID/revision -> test ID and baseline -> specs packet/revision -> code
commit -> passing result -> independent DoD review. The MMF remains one outcome containing multiple children.

This tests-before-packet sequence is a project proposal, not a claim about the upstream command order. The
[Flow-Forward guide](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/evolving-specs.html) normally creates the feature
specification before plan/tasks/implementation. Its preservation model still applies: retain the accepted
completed packet; use a linked new packet for a later substantial change. D-36 keeps canonical docs/specs/ living.

### Layer 3 — What Lane A must return; acceptance and refusal

1. Keep one BCP-1 map with separate intent, test-baseline, implementation-packet and result rows. Add phase,
   creation trigger, authority/test/code links and evidence state to the existing ownership/custody fields.

   refusal for wrong-scope tests, missing trace links, an unrelated failing run, or a green result without the
   required database/integration evidence. No automatic DoD or push follows a test pass.
5. Return one hash-bound design answer in B-136, covering the retained corrections and this delta. Lane B reviews
   it. Any new-root allocation/adoption needs its later D-54 rule/check/tier plan before creation; no execution now.

and .specify/ coverage must be assessed explicitly. Existing tool/runtime blockers keep their own triggers.
